john._voice_default: Charlie (premade, australian/male) - placeholder until John's clone is set up
john.style_notes: John Menagh, Progress. Overt optimist, plain-spoken, talks to the room in first-person inclusive 'we'/'us'. Vivid homely idioms, about one per key beat: 'their chickens have come home to roost', 'quaking in their slippers', 'the middle-man has left the building', 'gold from fool's gold', 'having a crack'. Folksy proverbs to open or punctuate. Punchy fragments for emphasis: 'Great. Interesting.' / 'Danger! Danger!' Rhetorical scene-setting questions. Clear signposting: opens beats with 'Right -', 'So', 'Now'. Outcome- and customer-empathy centred, challenges complacency gently and with humour. Australian spelling, no em dashes (spaced hyphens). Confident, never arrogant. Full profile: memory john-menagh-voice.

bill._voice_default: Bill - older American male (ElevenLabs premade, mature/measured/wry). Chosen 4 Sep 2026.
bill.style_notes: THE deadpan register voice: dry, measured, world-weary elder-statesman read that treats the trivial with total gravity - the comedic engine for understated, deadpan pieces (chosen for the Fanclub 'Ruling Engine' / Curb Your Enthusiasm cinematic trailer, deliberately distinct from Trek's Hope and SV's Will). Run at stability ~0.6, style 0.0 for a flat, unhurried delivery. Single voice throughout a piece; eleven_multilingual_v2. CAST 13 Oct 2026 for the demos/films/decks showreel (videos/showreel-2026-10), against a register brief of 'measured, dry, unhurried - a craft documentary, not a trailer'. Auditioned on two real narration lines against daniel (British broadcast) and david (the standing Australian default, auditioned rather than skipped per the note on that voice): measured 151.5 / 149.6 / 183.8 wpm, which separates david out and does NOT separate bill from daniel - so the choice between those two was made on the documented register above, and the builder stated plainly that it has no audio perception and cast on fit plus pace rather than on a listen. PACE LEVER, with voices.json's own two conditions met: the script was lead-locked and unrewritable, so writing-first was unavailable, and `speed` on eleven_multilingual_v2 was calibrated on the FULL 23-line set at 1.00 / 0.75 / 0.70 (170.0 / 128.3 / 118.9 wpm overall) rather than on a sample. 0.70 was taken, landing mid-window against the brief's 100-130. NOT resampling: pooled median f0 across the three speeds moved 147.1 to 136.2 Hz, where a resampling implementation at 0.70 would read about 103 Hz, and the 10.9 Hz across-speed spread is smaller than the 12.9 Hz between-take spread at a single speed - so it is estimator noise, not pitch. Settings for that build: stability 0.6, similarity 0.75, style 0.0, seed 20261013.

jay._voice_default: Brad - Australian narrator (placeholder until Jay's clone, e.g. JAY(ME!), is set up)
jay.style_notes: Jay Sanderson, default narrator and default content voice. Practitioner reporting back, not a pundit; enthusiastic but hype-allergic. Signature rhythm: short, punchy, deliberate fragments after a long sentence ('The model was never the hard part. Your context is.'). Cold open on a scene or claim, build to one memorable reframe, restate it tighter, close with a low-pressure collegial invitation. Always concede one honest caveat. Plain Anglo-Saxon words, gloss jargon in parentheses on first use, ground claims in concrete numbers. Dry humour, occasional deadpan ':)'. Australian spelling. Em dashes allowed in his personal LinkedIn/articles; spaced hyphens everywhere else. Full profile: memory jay-sanderson-voice.

david.style_notes: THE voice for anything targeted at an AUSTRALIAN audience (GM directive, 22 Aug 2026; RE-AFFIRMED 28 Sep 2026 after the GM rejected a tourism film cast on an audition winner - "go back to using David as that as an Australian sounding voice"). Treat this as the standing default for Australian-audience narration, not a candidate in an audition: an audition may still run to check register, but david only loses it if the GM himself says so. Single voice throughout a piece. Clear, professional register. Note the measured trade-off so it is handled in the WRITING, not by re-casting: david reads fast (171 wpm on the tourism opening lines). Where a piece wants gravitas, buy it with written-in pauses, shorter sentences and beat holds in the script rather than a slower voice. ADDENDUM (29 Sep 2026, Experience-co re-narration): that writing-first rule assumes the script is still writable. When BOTH the script and the picture are already locked - a re-narration of an approved cut, where 47 lines were each written to land on a visible beat - rewriting is not available, and the ElevenLabs `speed` parameter is then the legitimate lever. Measured on that build: david at natural speed ran about 9 per cent shorter than the approved read, and speed 0.95 put every line back on its authored frame (worst drift 0.35s, against 1.15s for the voice it replaced). Two conditions before using it: calibrate on the FULL line set, never a sample (a six-line calibration mispredicted the ratio and produced 0.85, which drifted 29 of 47 lines past a second), and confirm it is not resampling the voice - check median f0 across settings is unrelated to speed (measured 113-131 Hz with no relationship, so no pitch shift). Outside that locked-both-ends case the writing-first rule stands unchanged. Also measured on eleven_multilingual_v2 (and scoped to that model - scripts/voiceover.py documents seed as NON-reproducible on eleven_v3, untested): A FIXED SEED REPRODUCES THE TAKE TO WITHIN MEASUREMENT NOISE on every property you would re-roll for. Not bit-identical - three renders at one seed returned three different md5s - but identical byte length and duration, with speech-RMS moving only -24.96 to -24.97 dB and crest 23.27 to 23.46 across eight attempts. Varying the seed moved the same line across 3.1 dB of RMS and 0.79s of duration. So re-rolling WITHOUT changing the seed cannot move level, crest or duration, and any "we re-rolled it and it did not improve" conclusion drawn that way is unproven. A varied seed is necessary but NOT sufficient: 2 of 3 varied-seed renders came back at the same length, so a real re-roll needs several attempts. Known instance: rerender_uniform.py called synth_timed without previous_text/next_text, so its FIRST attempt per line genuinely differed from the original (that is where its variation came from) while attempts 2-7 at the unchanged seed were the same take again - its "6 of 23 lines clean in 7 attempts" is one real sample per line plus six repeats.

arthur.style_notes: THE big-room KEYNOTE voice: measured, authoritative, unhurried - cast for the Progress ISV partner keynote (60s ERP video) over Hope (explainer register, not a room), Andy (more drive, less authority) and Daniel (British gravitas but too slow for a 60s cut). Auditioned on the film's real opening lines: videos/erp-keynote/audition/. RE-AUDITIONED and re-confirmed 23 Sep 2026 for the 3.65-minute NARRATED ERP keynote cut, against three fresh shared-library American males on the same copy: arthur 149 wpm with 10 pauses in 18s (0.55/sec), Jonathan (warm executive narrator) 136 wpm, Russ (deep American narrator) 182 wpm, Ethan (conversational announcer) 181 wpm. Arthur wins for any film whose grammar is READ-THE-EVIDENCE: the pauses are the point, because the room needs time to read what is on screen, and the ~181 wpm reads either crowd the evidence or force you to stretch beats to manufacture air. Measured pace 2.38-2.49 words/sec, so size narration at ~130-150 words per minute of film. MODEL NOTE (23 Sep 2026): for a long narration rendered as many separate lines, use eleven_multilingual_v2, NOT eleven_v3 - v3 rejects previous_text/next_text outright, and 37 renders that must sound like one take need that continuity more than they need v3's audio tags. Per-line RMS normalisation before assembly is mandatory regardless: the 37 lines came back with a 9.5 LU raw spread. Use for partner/investor/keynote pieces aimed at a US or neutral-international room. Single voice throughout a piece.

mx_lazarus.style_notes: THE PERFORMANCE voice for the Molyneux Files / interview-archive register: a smoky, seasoned noir baritone - an archivist who has lived with the tapes, not a vampire and not a horror-trailer read. Cast after the GM rejected a Hope-narrated cut as "very clinical"; the lesson is that voice is CAST for an atmospheric piece, never defaulted to the explainer voice. Deliberately outside wb_blackwood's posh-British-sinister lane - Raymond, the obvious gothic pick, was one of Widow's Bay's own audition candidates, so casting him would have been a casting echo of the reference. Auditioned against Ingmar (intimate/whispery), Jones (true-crime documentary) and Aion Seeker (solemn, sorrowful). MEASURED: 103 wpm with 0.35 internal pauses per second, against Hope's 207 wpm on identical copy - so it reads at roughly HALF explainer pace. WORD-BUDGET CONSEQUENCE: budget about half the words you would write for an explainer. 128 words runs ~75s on this voice and ~37s on Hope. Write trailer copy with the pauses written in (present-tense fragments, ellipses) and let the read set the runtime; never pad the edit to reach length. Render on eleven_v3 at Natural stability 0.5 for audio-tag expressiveness, as the approved Widow's Bay trailer did. Single voice throughout a piece. Auditions: videos/molyneux-showcase/audition/.

bigbill.style_notes: THE keynote voice from 23 Sep 2026, replacing arthur for the narrated Progress ISV partner ERP keynote. British male, measured and confident. MEASURED ON THIS FACTORY'S OWN COPY (5 representative script lines, 62 words, eleven_multilingual_v2): it is a FAST reader and needs the speed lever pulled hard - 188 wpm at speed 1.0, 181 at 0.92, 160 at 0.85, 141 at 0.80, and it saturates below that (0.75 came back 145, i.e. no slower than 0.80). Run it at speed 0.82 for a keynote register near 148 wpm, which is where a room can read the evidence on screen while the line plays. Note the voice's own default settings carry speed 0.97, so it is faster still if you accept the default. Per-line RMS normalisation before assembly is mandatory as with every voice - the level lottery measured a 3.6 LU raw spread across 5 lines. Model: eleven_multilingual_v2, for previous_text/next_text continuity across many separate line renders. Accent note: British, so it is the right register for a UK or neutral-international room; the earlier ERP keynote brief specified an American read, and this supersedes that by the GM's own choice. Every take that speaks a proper noun is ASR-verified before it is kept (see videos/erp-keynote/narrate_reel.py) - the name lottery is per-render, not per-voice.
